name: Distal duplication 14q syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and cytogenetic diagnosis of distal 14q duplication

criteria.description: Identification of duplication involving distal region of chromosome 14q by karyotyping or chromosomal microarray
Presence of global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphisms including micrognathia, hypertelorism, and broad nasal bridge
Presence of congenital malformations such as cardiac defects or skeletal anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cytogenetic confirmation of distal 14q duplication plus presence of developmental delay and characteristic dysmorphic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing; clinical features support the diagnosis.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of the upper urinary tract

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible hypothyroidism on thyroid panel
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing scoliosis or other anomalies
Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
genetic: Chromosomal microarray or karyotype demonstrating duplication of distal 14q region
other: Developmental assessments confirming global developmental delay

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct facial features and higher prevalence of autism spectrum disorder
Presence of mosaic trisomy 14 with variable phenotype
May include growth retardation and skin pigmentation anomalies

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Molecular Cytogenetics of Distal 14q Duplications, Am J Med Genet A. 2015
Clinical features and genetic analysis of distal 14q duplication syndrome, Eur J Med Genet. 2018
